thread:
vivian: spotted a weird parse failure pattern on the new quant canary this morning. canary-bot: canary 27990 report -> https://infradash/canaries/27990  failure-rate=2.1% baseline=0.1% :warning:
otto: what are we seeing?
vivian: samples show a UTF-8 BOM (0xEFBBBF) or other leading multi-byte markers prepended before the JSON object occasionally. example: 
RESPONSE_PREVIEW: "\uFEFF{\"action\":\"create\",\"args\":{}}"
that leading BOM causes json parser to choke in a few lang runtimes.
larry: interesting. BOM at start often from file/stream encoding mismatches or decompressor boundary issues. did we change proxy gzip or any transport layer?
vivian: no transport changes. quant profile: per-channel int8 with tight clipping; batch-window reduced to 30ms. small/one-line toolcall responses are the most affected.
otto: could be our streaming reassembly hitting a partial multibyte char boundary, then our sanitizer or tokenizer later injects a replacement or BOM marker. we saw similar behavior with split UTF-8 sequences before.
canary-bot: alert meta: failure_mode=utf8-bom-prefix, model=zephyr-int8-canary-27990, rate=2.1%
larry: immediate mitigations:
- enable small scrub that strips common BOM and leading unicode marks (U+FEFF, U+FFFD) before parse (canary opt-in)
- enable 1% raw-chunk capture to reproduce reassembly path
- run kv-cache off vs on microbench to see if prefix reuse correlates
vivian: scrub PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/7988 - scrub preserves raw log and is idempotent.
otto: I'll run a 5k sample microbench and pay attention to first-token byte sequences. also add a unit in onboarding harness to simulate split multi-byte UTF-8 across chunks.
vivian: timeline: scrub deploy in 20m, microbench in parallel, follow-up 11:00 PT with results. keep thread for retro notes. :thumbsup:
